node.title: Re: Filehandles and CSV_XS (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
is not a filehandle, it's the <> [doc://perlop#I/O-Operators|I/O operator] (aka [doc://readline]) applied to the bareword filehandle DATA. $csv->getline(DATA) may work in your code because you don't have [doc://strict] turned on (which can cause [id://11145345|strange and hard-to-analyze bugs]), but since you should always [id://111088], you should use the glob notation to pass bareword filehandles as arguments, i.e. $csv->getline(*DATA). For files you open, nowadays you should always use lexical filehandles - [id://11102684].

Minor edits shortly after posting.

Update in response to your edit: Relevant reading is [doc://perlmod#Symbol-Tables], [doc://perldata#Typeglobs-and-Filehandles], and [doc://perlsub#Passing-Symbol-Table-Entries-(typeglobs)] (and [doc://perlref] for globrefs).
